name: Sextans Dwarf Spheroidal
tagline: A very faint Milky Way satellite 290,000 light-years out — one of the least luminous dwarf spheroidals in the halo.
history: The Sextans dwarf was found only in 1990 on UK Schmidt plates — a smear so faint it evaded the earlier sky surveys entirely. Its stars are old and metal-poor, and its exceptionally low surface brightness means its stellar content is dwarfed by the dark matter scaffolding holding it together. It is a representative of the faintest tail of galaxy formation, barely brighter than a rich globular cluster.
